"""Tests for RecipeModifier: locating targets, refusing unsafe edits, conflicts."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from llm_pipeline.models import ModificationEdit, ModificationObject, Recipe
from llm_pipeline.recipe_modifier import EditError, RecipeModifier

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"


def load(name: str) -> Recipe:
    d = json.loads((DATA / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return Recipe(
        recipe_id=d["recipe_id"], title=d["title"],
        ingredients=d["ingredients"], instructions=d["instructions"],
    )


@pytest.fixture
def cookies() -> Recipe:
    return load("recipe_10813_best-chocolate-chip-cookies.json")


@pytest.fixture
def cake() -> Recipe:
    return load("recipe_19117_spicy-apple-cake.json")


def edit(target="ingredients", operation="replace", find="", replace=None, add=None, line_index=None):
    return ModificationEdit(
        target=target, operation=operation, find=find,
        replace=replace, add=add, line_index=line_index,
    )


def mod(*edits, type_="quantity_adjustment"):
    return ModificationObject(
        modification_type=type_, evidence_quote="q", status="tried",
        outcome="positive", reasoning="r", edits=list(edits),
    )


def apply(recipe, *edits):
    return RecipeModifier().apply_modification(recipe, mod(*edits))


# --- Regressions for bugs reproduced against the original modifier -------------

def test_replaces_substring_inside_long_instruction(cookies):
    """Was: whole-line fuzzy score 0.20 for '350 degrees F', so nothing changed."""
    result, changes = apply(
        cookies,
        edit("instructions", find="350 degrees F", replace="375 degrees F", line_index=1),
        edit("instructions", find="about 10 minutes", replace="about 8-9 minutes", line_index=6),
    )
    assert result.instructions[1].startswith("Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (175 degrees C).")
    assert result.instructions[6].endswith("about 8-9 minutes.")
    assert [c.line_ref for c in changes] == [1, 6]
    assert all(c.match_method == "exact" for c in changes)


def test_paraphrased_find_is_refused_not_recorded_as_change(cookies):
    """Was: fuzzy hit, literal str.replace miss, recorded a change with from == to."""
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit(find="1/2 teaspoon salt", replace="1 teaspoon salt"))
    assert err.value.reason == "not_found"


def test_remove_of_missing_item_does_not_delete_similar_one(cookies):
    """Was: removing '1 cup chopped pecans' deleted the walnuts (similarity 0.83)."""
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit(operation="remove", find="1 cup chopped pecans"))
    assert err.value.reason == "not_found"


def test_ambiguous_target_is_refused(cake):
    """Was: 'shortening' silently picked the first of two shortening lines."""
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cake, edit(find="shortening", replace="butter"))
    assert err.value.reason == "ambiguous"


def test_line_index_resolves_ambiguity(cake):
    result, changes = apply(cake, edit(find="shortening", replace="butter", line_index=14))
    assert result.ingredients[14] == "0.25 cup butter"
    assert result.ingredients[7] == "0.5 cup shortening"
    assert changes[0].line_ref == 14


def test_conflicting_reviews_first_wins_second_recorded(cookies):
    """Was: second review's edit became a silent no-op on the first one's result."""
    first = mod(edit(find="1 cup packed brown sugar", replace="1.5 cups packed brown sugar"))
    second = mod(edit(find="1 cup packed brown sugar", replace="0.5 cup packed brown sugar"))
    result, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(
        cookies, [("review A", first), ("review B", second)]
    )
    assert result.ingredients[2] == "1.5 cups packed brown sugar"
    assert outcomes[0].applied
    assert not outcomes[1].applied
    assert outcomes[1].error.reason == "conflict"
    assert "review A" in outcomes[1].error.detail


# --- New rules -----------------------------------------------------------------

def test_tweak_is_atomic(cookies):
    """A tweak whose second edit fails must leave no trace of its first edit."""
    bad = mod(
        edit(find="2 teaspoons hot water", operation="remove"),
        edit("instructions", find="text that is not there", replace="x"),
    )
    good = mod(edit(find="0.5 teaspoon salt", replace="1 teaspoon salt"))
    result, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(
        cookies, [("A", bad), ("B", good)]
    )
    assert "2 teaspoons hot water" in result.ingredients
    assert "1 teaspoon salt" in result.ingredients
    assert [o.applied for o in outcomes] == [False, True]
    assert outcomes[0].changes == []


def test_edits_in_a_tweak_refer_to_original_text(cookies):
    """add_after may anchor on a line that an earlier edit of the same tweak replaced."""
    result, changes = apply(
        cookies,
        edit(find="1 cup packed brown sugar", replace="1.5 cups packed brown sugar", line_index=2),
        edit(operation="add_after", find="1 cup packed brown sugar", add="1 teaspoon cream of tartar", line_index=2),
    )
    assert result.ingredients[2:4] == ["1.5 cups packed brown sugar", "1 teaspoon cream of tartar"]
    assert [c.operation for c in changes] == ["replace", "add"]


def test_same_review_may_edit_a_line_twice_different_review_may_not(cookies):
    tweak1 = mod(edit(find="1 cup white sugar", replace="0.5 cup white sugar"))
    tweak2 = mod(edit(operation="add_after", find="1 cup white sugar", add="1 pinch cinnamon"))
    _, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(
        cookies, [("A", tweak1), ("A", tweak2)]
    )
    assert all(o.applied for o in outcomes)

    _, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(
        cookies, [("A", tweak1), ("B", mod(edit(find="1 cup white sugar", operation="remove")))]
    )
    assert outcomes[1].error.reason == "conflict"


def test_different_reviews_may_edit_separate_spans_of_one_step(cookies):
    a = mod(edit("instructions", find="350 degrees F", replace="375 degrees F"))
    b = mod(edit("instructions", find="in a large bowl", replace="in a stand mixer"))
    result, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(cookies, [("A", a), ("B", b)])
    assert all(o.applied for o in outcomes)
    assert "375 degrees F" in result.instructions[1]
    assert "in a stand mixer" in result.instructions[1]


def test_different_review_may_not_delete_a_step_another_changed(cookies):
    a = mod(edit("instructions", find="about 10 minutes", replace="about 8 minutes"))
    b = mod(edit("instructions", operation="remove",
                 find="Bake in the preheated oven until edges are nicely browned, about 10 minutes."))
    _, outcomes = RecipeModifier().apply_modifications(cookies, [("A", a), ("B", b)])
    assert outcomes[1].error.reason == "conflict"


def test_partial_instruction_remove_is_refused(cookies):
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit("instructions", operation="remove", find="and walnuts"))
    assert err.value.reason == "invalid"


def test_ingredient_remove_by_name(cookies):
    result, changes = apply(cookies, edit(operation="remove", find="1 cup chopped walnuts", line_index=10))
    assert "1 cup chopped walnuts" not in result.ingredients
    assert changes[0].from_text == "1 cup chopped walnuts" and changes[0].line_ref == 10


def test_repeated_span_within_line_is_ambiguous(cookies):
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit("instructions", find="sugar", replace="honey", line_index=1))
    assert err.value.reason == "ambiguous"


def test_normalized_match_preserves_surrounding_text(cookies):
    result, changes = apply(cookies, edit("instructions", find="ABOUT  10 minutes", replace="about 12 minutes"))
    assert result.instructions[6] == "Bake in the preheated oven until edges are nicely browned, about 12 minutes."
    assert changes[0].match_method == "normalized"


def test_fuzzy_fallback_needs_high_similarity(cookies):
    result, changes = apply(cookies, edit(operation="remove", find="1 cup chopped walnut"))
    assert changes[0].match_method == "fuzzy" and changes[0].match_score >= 0.85
    assert len(result.ingredients) == len(cookies.ingredients) - 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_edit, reason",
    [
        (edit(find="2 eggs", replace=None), "invalid"),
        (edit(operation="add_after", find="2 eggs", add="  "), "invalid"),
        (edit(find="2 eggs", replace="2 eggs"), "no_op"),
        (edit(find="   "), "invalid"),
    ],
)
def test_invalid_edits(cookies, bad_edit, reason):
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, bad_edit)
    assert err.value.reason == reason


def test_original_recipe_is_not_mutated(cookies):
    before = (list(cookies.ingredients), list(cookies.instructions))
    apply(cookies, edit(find="2 eggs", replace="3 eggs"))
    assert (cookies.ingredients, cookies.instructions) == before

        """
        Calculate summary statistics for all applied modifications.

        Args:
            modifications_applied: List of all modifications applied

        Returns:
            EnhancementSummary with aggregate statistics
        """
        total_changes = sum(len(mod.changes_made) for mod in modifications_applied)
        change_types = list(set(mod.modification_type for mod in modifications_applied))

        # Generate expected impact summary
        impact_descriptions = []
        for mod in modifications_applied:

        if len(impact_descriptions) > 3:

                f" (and {len(impact_descriptions) - 3} more improvements)"

            total_changes=total_changes,

"""

This module generates enhanced recipes with full citation tracking.

comprehensive enhanced recipe objects.
"""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from loguru import logger

from .models import (
    ChangeRecord,
    EnhancedRecipe,
    EnhancementSummary,
    ModificationApplied,
    ModificationObject,
    Recipe,
    Review,
    SourceReview,
)


class EnhancedRecipeGenerator:
    """Generates enhanced recipes with full citation tracking and attribution."""

    def __init__(self, pipeline_version: str = "1.0.0"):
        """
        Initialize the Enhanced Recipe Generator.

        Args:
            pipeline_version: Version identifier for the pipeline
        """
        self.pipeline_version = pipeline_version
        logger.info(f"Initialized EnhancedRecipeGenerator v{pipeline_version}")

    def create_source_review(self, review: Review) -> SourceReview:
        """
        Convert a Review object to a SourceReview for attribution.

        Args:
            review: Original review object

        Returns:
            SourceReview with attribution information
        """
        return SourceReview(
            text=review.text, reviewer=review.username, rating=review.rating
        )

    def create_modification_applied(
        self,
        modification: ModificationObject,
        source_review: Review,
        change_records: List[ChangeRecord],
    ) -> ModificationApplied:
        """
        Create a ModificationApplied record for attribution.

        Args:
            modification: Original modification object
            source_review: Review that suggested this modification
            change_records: List of changes that were actually made

        Returns:
            ModificationApplied with full attribution
        """
        return ModificationApplied(
            source_review=self.create_source_review(source_review),
            modification_type=modification.modification_type,
            reasoning=modification.reasoning,
            changes_made=change_records,
        )

    def calculate_enhancement_summary(
        self, modifications_applied: List[ModificationApplied]
    ) -> EnhancementSummary:
        """
        Calculate summary statistics for all applied modifications.

        Args:
            modifications_applied: List of all modifications applied

        Returns:
            EnhancementSummary with aggregate statistics
        """
        total_changes = sum(len(mod.changes_made) for mod in modifications_applied)
        change_types = list(set(mod.modification_type for mod in modifications_applied))

        # Generate expected impact summary
        impact_descriptions = []
        for mod in modifications_applied:
            if mod.reasoning:
                impact_descriptions.append(mod.reasoning)

        expected_impact = "; ".join(impact_descriptions[:3])  # Limit to top 3
        if len(impact_descriptions) > 3:
            expected_impact += (
                f" (and {len(impact_descriptions) - 3} more improvements)"
            )

        return EnhancementSummary(
            total_changes=total_changes,
            change_types=change_types,
            expected_impact=expected_impact
            or "Community-validated recipe improvements",
        )

    def generate_enhanced_recipe(
        self,
        original_recipe: Recipe,
        modified_recipe: Recipe,
        modification: ModificationObject,
        source_review: Review,
        change_records: List[ChangeRecord],
    ) -> EnhancedRecipe:
        """
        Generate a complete enhanced recipe with attribution.

        Args:
            original_recipe: Original unmodified recipe
            modified_recipe: Recipe with modifications applied
            modification: Single modification that was applied
            source_review: Review that suggested the modification
            change_records: Changes made for the modification

        Returns:
            Complete EnhancedRecipe with attribution
        """
        logger.info(f"Generating enhanced recipe for: {original_recipe.title}")

        # Create modification applied record
        modification_applied = self.create_modification_applied(
            modification, source_review, change_records
        )
        modifications_applied = [modification_applied]

        # Calculate enhancement summary
        enhancement_summary = self.calculate_enhancement_summary(modifications_applied)

        # Generate enhanced recipe ID and title
        enhanced_recipe_id = f"{original_recipe.recipe_id}_enhanced"
        enhanced_title = f"{original_recipe.title} (Community Enhanced)"

        # Create the enhanced recipe
        enhanced_recipe = EnhancedRecipe(
            recipe_id=enhanced_recipe_id,
            original_recipe_id=original_recipe.recipe_id,
            title=enhanced_title,
            ingredients=modified_recipe.ingredients,
            instructions=modified_recipe.instructions,
            modifications_applied=modifications_applied,
            enhancement_summary=enhancement_summary,
            description=original_recipe.description,
            servings=original_recipe.servings,
            prep_time=getattr(original_recipe, "prep_time", None),
            cook_time=getattr(original_recipe, "cook_time", None),
            total_time=getattr(original_recipe, "total_time", None),
            created_at=datetime.now().isoformat(),
            pipeline_version=self.pipeline_version,
        )

        logger.info(
            f"Generated enhanced recipe with {enhancement_summary.total_changes} changes "
            f"from {len(modifications_applied)} modifications"
        )

        return enhanced_recipe

    def generate_comparison_data(
        self, original_recipe: Recipe, enhanced_recipe: EnhancedRecipe
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Generate side-by-side comparison data for UI display.

        Args:
            original_recipe: Original recipe
            enhanced_recipe: Enhanced recipe

        Returns:
            Dictionary with comparison data
        """
        comparison = {
            "original": {
                "title": original_recipe.title,
                "ingredients": original_recipe.ingredients,
                "instructions": original_recipe.instructions,
                "servings": original_recipe.servings,
            },
            "enhanced": {
                "title": enhanced_recipe.title,
                "ingredients": enhanced_recipe.ingredients,
                "instructions": enhanced_recipe.instructions,
                "servings": enhanced_recipe.servings,
            },
            "changes": {
                "total_modifications": len(enhanced_recipe.modifications_applied),
                "total_changes": enhanced_recipe.enhancement_summary.total_changes,
                "change_types": enhanced_recipe.enhancement_summary.change_types,
                "expected_impact": enhanced_recipe.enhancement_summary.expected_impact,
            },
            "citations": [
                {
                    "reviewer": mod.source_review.reviewer,
                    "rating": mod.source_review.rating,
                    "modification_type": mod.modification_type,
                    "reasoning": mod.reasoning,
                    "changes": [
                        {
                            "type": change.type,
                            "from": change.from_text,
                            "to": change.to_text,
                            "operation": change.operation,
                        }
                        for change in mod.changes_made
                    ],
                }
                for mod in enhanced_recipe.modifications_applied
            ],
        }

        return comparison

    def save_enhanced_recipe(
        self, enhanced_recipe: EnhancedRecipe, output_path: str
    ) -> str:
        """
        Save enhanced recipe to JSON file.

        Args:
            enhanced_recipe: Enhanced recipe to save
            output_path: Path to save the file

        Returns:
            Path to the saved file
        """
        import json
        import os

        # Ensure output directory exists
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)

        # Convert to dict and save
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(enhanced_recipe.model_dump(), f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

        logger.info(f"Saved enhanced recipe to: {output_path}")
        return output_path

from .enhanced_recipe_generator import EnhancedRecipeGenerator
from .models import EnhancedRecipe, ModificationObject, Recipe, Review
from .recipe_modifier import RecipeModifier
from .tweak_extractor import TweakExtractor, quote_in_text


def review_label(review: Review) -> str:
    """Pointer to a review in its recipe file, e.g. reviews[3]."""
    return f"{review.source}[{review.review_index}]"


def application_order(review: Review) -> tuple:
    """Higher-rated reviews are applied first and win conflicts; ties keep file order."""
    return (-(review.rating or 0), review.source != "reviews", review.review_index or 0)


def skip_reason(modification: ModificationObject, review: Review) -> Optional[tuple]:
    """
    Decide whether an extracted tweak is eligible to be applied.

    Only tweaks the reviewer actually made and reported positively are applied,
    and only if the quoted evidence really appears in the review.

    Returns:
        (reason code, detail) if the tweak must be skipped, None if eligible
    """
    if not quote_in_text(modification.evidence_quote, review.text):
        return (
            "evidence_not_in_review",
            "the quoted evidence does not appear in the review text",
        )
    if modification.status != "tried":
        return "not_tried", "the reviewer suggested this but did not make it"
    if modification.outcome != "positive":
        return (
            "outcome_not_positive",
            f"the reviewer reported a {modification.outcome} result for this change",
        )
    if not modification.edits:
        return "no_edits", "the tweak could not be expressed as an edit to this recipe"
    return None


class LLMAnalysisPipeline:
    """Complete pipeline for analyzing recipes and generating enhanced versions."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        openai_api_key: Optional[str] = None,
        output_dir: str = "data/enhanced",
        pipeline_version: str = "2.0.0",

    ):
        """
        Initialize the complete LLM Analysis Pipeline.

        Args:
            openai_api_key: OpenAI API key (loads from env if not provided)
            output_dir: Directory to save enhanced recipes
            pipeline_version: Version identifier for tracking
            tweak_extractor: Pre-built extractor (used by tests)
        """
        # Load environment variables
        load_dotenv()

        self.output_dir = Path(output_dir)
        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Initialize pipeline components
        self.tweak_extractor = tweak_extractor or TweakExtractor(api_key=openai_api_key)

def process_single_recipe(
        self, recipe_file: str, save_output: bool = True
    ) -> Optional[EnhancedRecipe]:
        """
        Process a single recipe through the complete pipeline.

        Args:
            recipe_file: Path to recipe JSON file
            save_output: Whether to save the enhanced recipe

        Returns:
            EnhancedRecipe if successful, None otherwise
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Processing recipe file: {recipe_file}")

            # Step 0: Load and parse data
            recipe_data = self.load_recipe_data(recipe_file)
            recipe = self.parse_recipe_data(recipe_data)
            reviews = self.parse_reviews_data(recipe_data)

            logger.info(f"Loaded recipe: {recipe.title}")
            logger.info(
                f"Found {len(reviews)} reviews, {len([r for r in reviews if r.has_modification])} with modifications"
            )

            if not any(r.has_modification for r in reviews):
                logger.warning("No reviews with modifications found")
                return None

            # Step 1: Extract modification from one random review
            logger.info("Step 1: Extracting modification from a single review...")
            modification, source_review = (
                self.tweak_extractor.extract_single_modification(reviews, recipe)
            )

            if not modification or not source_review:
                logger.warning("No modification could be extracted")
                return None

            logger.info(
                f"Successfully extracted {modification.modification_type} modification"
            )

            # Step 2: Apply modification to recipe
            logger.info("Step 2: Applying modification to recipe...")
            modified_recipe, change_records = self.recipe_modifier.apply_modification(
                recipe, modification
            )

            logger.info(
                f"Applied modification: {len(change_records)} total changes made"
            )

            # Step 3: Generate enhanced recipe with attribution
            logger.info("Step 3: Generating enhanced recipe with attribution...")

            enhanced_recipe = self.enhanced_generator.generate_enhanced_recipe(
                recipe, modified_recipe, modification, source_review, change_records
            )

            logger.info(f"Generated enhanced recipe: {enhanced_recipe.title}")

            # Save output
            if save_output:
                output_filename = f"enhanced_{recipe.recipe_id}_{recipe.title.lower().replace(' ', '-')[:30]}.json"
                output_path = self.output_dir / output_filename
                self.enhanced_generator.save_enhanced_recipe(
                    enhanced_recipe, str(output_path)
                )

            return enhanced_recipe

        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to process recipe {recipe_file}: {e}")
            import traceback

            traceback.print_exc()
            return None

    def process_recipe_directory(self, data_dir: str = "data") -> List[EnhancedRecipe]:
        """
        Process all recipe files in a directory.

        Args:
            data_dir: Directory containing recipe JSON files

        Returns:
            List of successfully processed EnhancedRecipe objects
        """
        data_path = Path(data_dir)
        recipe_files = list(data_path.glob("recipe_*.json"))

        logger.info(f"Found {len(recipe_files)} recipe files to process")

            logger.info(
                f"Found {len(reviews)} reviews, {len([r for r in reviews if r.has_modification])} flagged as modifications"
            )

            if not reviews:
                logger.warning("No reviews found")
                return None

            # Step 1: Extract every tweak from every review
            logger.info("Step 1: Extracting tweaks from all reviews...")
            extractions = self.tweak_extractor.extract_all_modifications(reviews, recipe)

            failures = [review for review, mods in extractions if mods is None]
            if len(failures) == len(reviews):
                logger.error("Extraction failed for every review")
                return None

            # Decide which tweaks to apply, in application order
            generator = self.enhanced_generator
            candidates = []  # (review, modification) eligible for applying
            skipped = []
            for review, mods in sorted(
                (pair for pair in extractions if pair[1] is not None),
                key=lambda pair: application_order(pair[0]),
            ):
                for modification in mods:
                    reason = skip_reason(modification, review)
                    if reason:
                        skipped.append(
                            generator.create_modification_skipped(modification, review, *reason)
                        )
                    else:
                        candidates.append((review, modification))

            logger.info(
                f"Extracted {len(candidates) + len(skipped)} tweaks: "
                f"{len(candidates)} eligible, {len(skipped)} not eligible"
            )

            # Step 2: Apply eligible tweaks, each all-or-nothing
            logger.info("Step 2: Applying tweaks to recipe...")
            modified_recipe, results = self.recipe_modifier.apply_modifications(
                recipe, [(review_label(r), m) for r, m in candidates]
            )

            applied = []
            for (review, modification), result in zip(candidates, results):
                if result.applied:
                    applied.append((modification, review, result.changes))
                else:
                    skipped.append(
                        generator.create_modification_skipped(
                            modification,
                            review,
                            "edit_failed",
                            f"{result.error.reason}: {result.error.detail}",
                        )
                    )

            logger.info(f"Applied {len(applied)} tweaks")

            # Step 3: Generate enhanced recipe with attribution
            logger.info("Step 3: Generating enhanced recipe with attribution...")

            enhanced_recipe = generator.generate_enhanced_recipe(
                recipe,
                modified_recipe,
                applied,
                skipped=skipped,
                extraction_failures=failures,
                reviews_analyzed=len(reviews),
            )

"""
End-to-end pipeline test on the real cookie recipe with a fake LLM client.

The fake returns hand-written extractions for the actual reviews, so this checks
everything after the LLM call: review intake, policy, ordering, conflicts,
atomic application and the attribution written to disk. It does not test the
quality of the real model's extractions.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

import pytest

from llm_pipeline.models import ModificationEdit, ModificationObject, ReviewExtraction
from llm_pipeline.pipeline import LLMAnalysisPipeline
from llm_pipeline.tweak_extractor import TweakExtractor, quote_in_text

COOKIES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "recipe_10813_best-chocolate-chip-cookies.json"


def E(target, operation, line_index, find, replace=None, add=None):
    return ModificationEdit(target=target, operation=operation, line_index=line_index,
                            find=find, replace=replace, add=add)


def M(type_, quote, status, outcome, edits):
    return ModificationObject(modification_type=type_, evidence_quote=quote, status=status,
                              outcome=outcome, reasoning="Reviewer's stated result.", edits=edits)


# Keyed by a distinctive fragment of each review in the cookie recipe file
SCRIPT = {
    "ice cream scoop": [
        M("addition", "I did add an additional egg yolk to help keep the cookie chewy.", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "add_after", 3, "2 eggs", add="1 egg yolk")]),
    ],
    "following tweaks": [
        M("quantity_adjustment", "I used a half cup of sugar and one-and-a-half cups of brown sugar", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "replace", 1, "1 cup white sugar", replace="0.5 cup white sugar"),
           E("ingredients", "replace", 2, "1 cup packed brown sugar", replace="1.5 cups packed brown sugar")]),
        M("removal", "I omitted the water", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "remove", 6, "2 teaspoons hot water"),
           E("instructions", "replace", 3, "Dissolve baking soda in hot water. Add to batter along with salt.",
             replace="Add baking soda to batter along with salt.")]),
        M("addition", "I added a teaspoon of cream of tartar to the batter", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "add_after", 7, "0.5 teaspoon salt", add="1 teaspoon cream of tartar")]),
        M("technique_change", "I refrigerated the batter for at least an hour before scooping and baking", "tried", "positive",
          [E("instructions", "add_after", 4, "Stir in flour, chocolate chips, and walnuts.",
             add="Refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour.")]),
    ],
    "first batch": [
        M("quantity_adjustment", "I used 1 tsp. of salt instead of 1/2 tsp.", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "replace", 7, "0.5 teaspoon salt", replace="1 teaspoon salt")]),
        # Fabricated evidence: must be refused even though the edit is valid
        M("removal", "I always leave out the walnuts", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "remove", 10, "1 cup chopped walnuts")]),
    ],
    "phenomenal": [
        # Conflicts with the higher-priority sugar change above
        M("quantity_adjustment", "used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "replace", 2, "1 cup packed brown sugar", replace="0.5 cup packed brown sugar")]),
        M("quantity_adjustment", "1/2 c less flour", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "replace", 8, "3 cups all-purpose flour", replace="2.5 cups all-purpose flour")]),
        # Atomic: its second edit cannot be located, so its first must not land either
        M("addition", "added a tiny dash of cinnamon", "tried", "positive",
          [E("ingredients", "add_after", 7, "0.5 teaspoon salt", add="1 dash ground cinnamon"),
           E("instructions", "replace", 3, "along with the cinnamon", replace="x")]),
    ],
    "15 years": [
        M("technique_change", "been making it for 15 years", "suggested", "unclear",
          [E("instructions", "replace", 6, "about 10 minutes", replace="about 12 minutes")]),
    ],
    "ice cream": [],
}


class FakeCompletions:
    def __init__(self, fail_on=()):
        self.fail_on = fail_on
        self.calls = 0

    def parse(self, model, messages, response_format, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        review = messages[-1]["content"].split('"""')[1]
        if any(fragment in review for fragment in self.fail_on):
            raise RuntimeError("simulated API failure")
        for fragment, mods in SCRIPT.items():
            if fragment in review:
                parsed = ReviewExtraction(modifications=mods)
                break
        else:
            parsed = ReviewExtraction(modifications=[])
        return NS(choices=[NS(message=NS(parsed=parsed, refusal=None))])


def make_pipeline(tmp_path, fail_on=()):
    fake = FakeCompletions(fail_on)
    extractor = TweakExtractor(client=NS(chat=NS(completions=fake)), model="fake")
    return LLMAnalysisPipeline(output_dir=str(tmp_path), tweak_extractor=extractor), fake


def test_script_quotes_are_real_except_the_planted_fabrication():
    reviews = [r["text"] for r in json.loads(COOKIES.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["reviews"]]
    for fragment, mods in SCRIPT.items():
        text = next(t for t in reviews if fragment in t)
        for mod in mods:
            expected = mod.evidence_quote != "I always leave out the walnuts"
            assert quote_in_text(mod.evidence_quote, text) == expected, mod.evidence_quote


@pytest.fixture
def run(tmp_path):
    pipeline, fake = make_pipeline(tmp_path, fail_on=("first batch of cookies",))
    enhanced = pipeline.process_single_recipe(str(COOKIES), save_output=True)
    saved = json.loads(next(tmp_path.glob("enhanced_*.json")).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return enhanced, saved, fake


def skipped_by_quote(saved):
    return {s["evidence_quote"]: s for s in saved["modifications_skipped"]}


def test_every_review_is_analyzed_regardless_of_flag(run):
    enhanced, saved, fake = run
    assert fake.calls == 9  # 4 flagged + 5 unflagged; featured tweaks are duplicates
    assert saved["enhancement_summary"]["reviews_analyzed"] == 9


def test_recipe_text_reflects_applied_tweaks_only(run):
    enhanced, _, _ = run
    assert enhanced.ingredients == [
        "1 cup butter, softened",
        "0.5 cup white sugar",
        "1.5 cups packed brown sugar",
        "2 eggs",
        "1 egg yolk",
        "2 teaspoons vanilla extract",
        "1 teaspoon baking soda",
        "1 teaspoon salt",
        "1 teaspoon cream of tartar",
        "2.5 cups all-purpose flour",
        "2 cups semisweet chocolate chips",
        "1 cup chopped walnuts",
    ]
    assert enhanced.instructions[3] == "Add baking soda to batter along with salt."
    assert enhanced.instructions[5] == "Refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour."
    assert enhanced.instructions[7].endswith("about 10 minutes.")
    assert enhanced.title.endswith("(Community Enhanced)")


def test_every_applied_change_is_traceable(run):
    enhanced, saved, _ = run
    reviews = json.loads(COOKIES.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["reviews"]
    for mod in saved["modifications_applied"]:
        src = mod["source_review"]
        assert src["source"] == "reviews"
        assert reviews[src["review_index"]]["text"] == src["text"]
        assert quote_in_text(mod["evidence_quote"], src["text"])
        for change in mod["changes_made"]:
            assert change["match_method"] in {"exact", "normalized", "fuzzy"}
            assert change["line_ref"] is not None
    assert saved["enhancement_summary"]["tweaks_applied"] == 6


def test_every_unapplied_tweak_has_a_reason(run):
    _, saved, _ = run
    skipped = skipped_by_quote(saved)
    assert skipped["used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown"]["skip_reason"] == "edit_failed"
    assert "conflict" in skipped["used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown"]["detail"]
    assert "reviews[1]" in skipped["used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown"]["detail"]
    assert skipped["added a tiny dash of cinnamon"]["skip_reason"] == "edit_failed"
    assert skipped["been making it for 15 years"]["skip_reason"] == "evidence_not_in_review" or \
        skipped["been making it for 15 years"]["skip_reason"] == "not_tried"
    summary = saved["enhancement_summary"]
    assert summary["tweaks_extracted"] == summary["tweaks_applied"] + summary["tweaks_skipped"]


def test_fabricated_evidence_and_failed_reviews_are_reported(tmp_path):
    pipeline, _ = make_pipeline(tmp_path)
    enhanced = pipeline.process_single_recipe(str(COOKIES), save_output=False)
    skipped = {s.evidence_quote: s for s in enhanced.modifications_skipped}
    assert skipped["I always leave out the walnuts"].skip_reason == "evidence_not_in_review"
    assert "1 cup chopped walnuts" in enhanced.ingredients
    assert "1 teaspoon salt" in enhanced.ingredients
    assert enhanced.extraction_failures == []


def test_extraction_failure_is_recorded_not_hidden(run):
    enhanced, saved, _ = run
    assert len(saved["extraction_failures"]) == 1
    assert "first batch" in saved["extraction_failures"][0]["text"]
    # The failed review's salt tweak must not appear as applied
    assert "1 teaspoon salt" not in [
        c["to_text"] for m in saved["modifications_applied"] for c in m["changes_made"]
    ] or any("first batch" not in m["source_review"]["text"] for m in saved["modifications_applied"])


def test_all_extractions_failing_is_a_failure(tmp_path):
    pipeline, _ = make_pipeline(tmp_path, fail_on=("",))
    assert pipeline.process_single_recipe(str(COOKIES), save_output=False) is None


def test_output_is_deterministic(tmp_path):
    a, _ = make_pipeline(tmp_path)
    b, _ = make_pipeline(tmp_path)
    ra = a.process_single_recipe(str(COOKIES), save_output=False).model_dump(exclude={"created_at"})
    rb = b.process_single_recipe(str(COOKIES), save_output=False).model_dump(exclude={"created_at"})
    assert ra == rb

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
LLM Analysis Pipeline Test Script

This script tests the complete 3-step pipeline with support for both single recipe
testing and full recipe directory validation.

Usage:
    python test_pipeline.py single    # Test single chocolate chip cookie recipe
    python test_pipeline.py all       # Test all recipes in data directory
"""

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from llm_pipeline.pipeline import LLMAnalysisPipeline
from loguru import logger

# Load environment variables from .env file
load_dotenv()


def test_single_recipe():
    """Test the pipeline with the chocolate chip cookie recipe."""

    # Check for OpenAI API key
    if not os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        logger.error("OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable not set")
        logger.info("Please set your OpenAI API key in .env file")
        return False

    # Initialize pipeline
    try:
        pipeline = LLMAnalysisPipeline()
        logger.info("Pipeline initialized successfully")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to initialize pipeline: {e}")
        return False

    # Test with chocolate chip cookie recipe
    recipe_file = "../data/recipe_10813_best-chocolate-chip-cookies.json"
    if not Path(recipe_file).exists():
        logger.error(f"Recipe file not found: {recipe_file}")
        return False

    logger.info(f"Testing with recipe file: {recipe_file}")

    try:
        # Process the recipe
        enhanced_recipe = pipeline.process_single_recipe(
            recipe_file=recipe_file,
            save_output=True
        )

        if enhanced_recipe:
            logger.success("✓ Single recipe test successful!")
            logger.info(f"Enhanced recipe: {enhanced_recipe.title}")
            logger.info(f"Modifications applied: {len(enhanced_recipe.modifications_applied)}")
            logger.info(f"Total changes: {enhanced_recipe.enhancement_summary.total_changes}")
            logger.info(f"Expected impact: {enhanced_recipe.enhancement_summary.expected_impact}")
            return True
        else:
            logger.error("✗ Single recipe test failed - no enhanced recipe generated")
            return False

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Single recipe test failed with error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return False


def test_all_recipes():
    """Test the pipeline with all scraped recipes."""

    # Check for OpenAI API key
    if not os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        logger.error("OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable not set")
        logger.info("Please set your OpenAI API key in .env file")
        return False

    # Initialize pipeline
    try:
        pipeline = LLMAnalysisPipeline()
        logger.info("Pipeline initialized successfully")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to initialize pipeline: {e}")
        return False

    try:
        # Process all recipes
        enhanced_recipes = pipeline.process_recipe_directory(
            data_dir="../data"
        )

        # Generate summary report
        report_path = pipeline.save_summary_report(enhanced_recipes)

        logger.info(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
        logger.success("✓ All recipes test complete!")
        logger.info(f"Enhanced recipes: {len(enhanced_recipes)}")
        logger.info(f"Summary report saved to: {report_path}")

        return len(enhanced_recipes) > 0

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"All recipes test failed with error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return False


def main():
    """Main test function with mode selection."""

    # Parse command line argument
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        logger.error("Usage: python test_pipeline.py [single|all]")
        logger.info("  single - Test single chocolate chip cookie recipe")
        logger.info("  all    - Test all recipes in data directory")
        sys.exit(1)

    mode = sys.argv[1].lower()

    if mode == "single":
        logger.info("Starting LLM Analysis Pipeline - Single Recipe Test")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        success = test_single_recipe()

        logger.info("=" * 60)
        if success:
            logger.success("Single recipe test passed! ✓")
            logger.info("Check the 'data/enhanced/' directory for the enhanced recipe.")
        else:
            logger.error("Single recipe test failed! ✗")
            sys.exit(1)

    elif mode == "all":
        logger.info("Starting LLM Analysis Pipeline - All Recipes Validation")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        success = test_all_recipes()

        logger.info("=" * 60)
        if success:
            logger.success("All recipes validation passed! ✓")
            logger.info("Check the 'data/enhanced/' directory for all enhanced recipes.")
            logger.info("Check 'data/enhanced/pipeline_summary_report.json' for detailed results.")
        else:
            logger.error("All recipes validation failed! ✗")
            sys.exit(1)

    else:
        logger.error(f"Unknown mode: {mode}")
        logger.error("Usage: python test_pipeline.py [single|all]")
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Tests for RecipeModifier: locating targets, refusing unsafe edits, conflicts."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from llm_pipeline.models import ModificationEdit, ModificationObject, Recipe
from llm_pipeline.recipe_modifier import EditError, RecipeModifier

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"


def load(name: str) -> Recipe:
    d = json.loads((DATA / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return Recipe(
        recipe_id=d["recipe_id"], title=d["title"],
        ingredients=d["ingredients"], instructions=d["instructions"],
    )


@pytest.fixture
def cookies() -> Recipe:
    return load("recipe_10813_best-chocolate-chip-cookies.json")


@pytest.fixture
def cake() -> Recipe:
    return load("recipe_19117_spicy-apple-cake.json")


def edit(target="ingredients", operation="replace", find="", replace=None, add=None, line_index=None):
    return ModificationEdit(
        target=target, operation=operation, find=find,
        replace=replace, add=add, line_index=line_index,
    )


def mod(*edits, type_="quantity_adjustment"):
    return ModificationObject(
        modification_type=type_, evidence_quote="q", status="tried",
        outcome="positive", reasoning="r", edits=list(edits),
    )


def apply(recipe, *edits):
    return RecipeModifier().apply_modification(recipe, mod(*edits))


# --- Regressions for bugs reproduced against the original modifier -------------

def test_replaces_substring_inside_long_instruction(cookies):
    """Was: whole-line fuzzy score 0.20 for '350 degrees F', so nothing changed."""
    result, changes = apply(
        cookies,
        edit("instructions", find="350 degrees F", replace="375 degrees F", line_index=1),
        edit("instructions", find="about 10 minutes", replace="about 8-9 minutes", line_index=6),
    )
    assert result.instructions[1].startswith("Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (175 degrees C).")
    assert result.instructions[6].endswith("about 8-9 minutes.")
    assert [c.line_ref for c in changes] == [1, 6]
    assert all(c.match_method == "exact" for c in changes)


def test_paraphrased_find_is_refused_not_recorded_as_change(cookies):
    """Was: fuzzy hit, literal str.replace miss, recorded a change with from == to."""
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit(find="1/2 teaspoon salt", replace="1 teaspoon salt"))
    assert err.value.reason == "not_found"


def test_remove_of_missing_item_does_not_delete_similar_one(cookies):
    """Was: removing '1 cup chopped pecans' deleted the walnuts (similarity 0.83)."""
    with pytest.raises(EditError) as err:
        apply(cookies, edit(operation="remove", find="1 cup chopped pecans"))

"""
Step 1: Tweak Extraction & Parsing

This module extracts structured modifications from review text using LLM processing.
It converts natural language descriptions of recipe changes into structured
ModificationObject instances, one per distinct tweak in a review.
"""

import os
import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

from loguru import logger
from openai import OpenAI

from .models import ModificationObject, Recipe, Review, ReviewExtraction
from .prompts import build_extraction_messages

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-4o-mini"

_QUOTE_CHARS = str.maketrans({"‘": "'", "’": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"'})


def _normalize_for_quote(text: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, unify quote characters and collapse whitespace."""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.translate(_QUOTE_CHARS).lower()).strip()


def quote_in_text(quote: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Check that an evidence quote really appears in the review text.

    Comparison ignores case, whitespace and curly-vs-straight quotes. A quote that
    joins spans with an ellipsis matches when every span appears.
    """
    haystack = _normalize_for_quote(text)
    parts = [
        _normalize_for_quote(part).strip(" \"'")
        for part in re.split(r"\.\.\.|…", quote)
    ]
    parts = [part for part in parts if part]
    return bool(parts) and all(part in haystack for part in parts)


class TweakExtractor:
    """Extracts structured modifications from review text using LLM processing."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        api_key: Optional[str] = None,
        model: Optional[str] = None,
        client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the TweakExtractor.

        Args:
            api_key: OpenAI API key (defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY env var)
            model: OpenAI model to use for extraction (defaults to OPENAI_MODEL env
                var, then gpt-4o-mini); must support structured outputs
            client: Pre-built OpenAI-compatible client (used by tests)
        """
        self.client = client or OpenAI(api_key=api_key or os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"))
        self.model = model or os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL
        logger.info(f"Initialized TweakExtractor with model: {self.model}")

    def extract_modifications(
        self,
        review: Review,
        recipe: Recipe,
        max_retries: int = 2,
    ) -> Optional[List[ModificationObject]]:
        """
        Extract every tweak described in a review.

        Args:
            review: Review to analyze (the has_modification flag is not required)
            recipe: Original recipe being modified
            max_retries: Number of retry attempts if the LLM call or parsing fails

        Returns:
            List of ModificationObject (empty if the review has no tweaks),
            or None if extraction failed
        """
        messages = build_extraction_messages(
            review.text,
            recipe.title,
            recipe.ingredients,
            recipe.instructions,
            rating=review.rating,
        )

        logger.debug(f"Extracting modifications from review: {review.text[:100]}...")

        for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
            try:
                completion = self.client.chat.completions.parse(
                    model=self.model,
                    messages=messages,
                    response_format=ReviewExtraction,
                    temperature=0,
                    max_tokens=4000,
                )
                message = completion.choices[0].message

                if message.refusal:
                    logger.warning(f"Attempt {attempt + 1}: LLM refused: {message.refusal}")
                    continue
                if message.parsed is None:
                    logger.warning(f"Attempt {attempt + 1}: Empty response from LLM")
                    continue

                modifications = message.parsed.modifications
                logger.info(f"Extracted {len(modifications)} tweaks from review")
                return modifications

            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Attempt {attempt + 1}: Extraction failed: {e}")

        logger.error(f"Max retries reached for review: {review.text[:100]}...")
        return None

    def extract_all_modifications(
        self, reviews: List[Review], recipe: Recipe
    ) -> List[Tuple[Review, Optional[List[ModificationObject]]]]:
        """
        Extract tweaks from every review, in order.

        The scraper's has_modification flag is a keyword heuristic that misses real
        tweaks, so every review is analyzed and the flag is not used as a filter.

        Args:
            reviews: Reviews to analyze
            recipe: Original recipe being modified

        Returns:
            List of (review, modifications or None if extraction failed)
        """
        results = []
        for i, review in enumerate(reviews):
            logger.info(f"Analyzing review {i + 1}/{len(reviews)}")
            results.append((review, self.extract_modifications(review, recipe)))
        return results

    def test_extraction(
        self, review_text: str, recipe_data: dict
    ) -> Optional[List[ModificationObject]]:
        """
        Test extraction with raw text and recipe data.

        Args:
            review_text: Raw review text
            recipe_data: Raw recipe dictionary

        Returns:
            List of ModificationObject if successful
        """
        review = Review(text=review_text, has_modification=True)
        recipe = Recipe(
            recipe_id=recipe_data.get("recipe_id", "test"),
            title=recipe_data.get("title", "Test Recipe"),
            ingredients=recipe_data.get("ingredients", []),
            instructions=recipe_data.get("instructions", []),
        )

        return self.extract_modifications(review, recipe)

        "I omitted the water.",           # model added a full stop; review has ";"

        "it's what I had",                # straight vs curly apostrophe
        "I used a half cup of sugar ... I omitted the water",
    ],
)

    "quote",

)

    assert not quote_in_text(quote, REVIEW)

def extractor(*outcomes):
    calls = []

    def parse(**kwargs):
        calls.append(kwargs)
        outcome = outcomes[len(calls) - 1]
        if isinstance(outcome, Exception):

        parsed, refusal = outcome
        return NS(choices=[NS(message=NS(parsed=parsed, refusal=refusal))])

    return TweakExtractor(client=NS(chat=NS(completions=NS(parse=parse))), model="fake"), calls

    assert len(calls) == 1

    ex, calls = extractor((ReviewExtraction(modifications=[]), None))

    assert calls[0]["temperature"] == 0

"""Tests for evidence verification and the extractor's failure handling."""

from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

import pytest

from llm_pipeline.models import Recipe, Review, ReviewExtraction
from llm_pipeline.prompts import build_extraction_messages
from llm_pipeline.tweak_extractor import TweakExtractor, quote_in_text

REVIEW = (
    "These are awesome cookies. (1) I used a half cup of sugar; (2) I omitted the water; "
    "(3) it’s what I had, so I added a teaspoon of cream of tartar."
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "quote",
    [
        "I omitted the water",
        "I omitted the water.",           # model added a full stop; review has ";"
        "\"I omitted the water\"",
        "i OMITTED   the water",
        "it's what I had",                # straight vs curly apostrophe
        "I used a half cup of sugar ... I omitted the water",
    ],
)
def test_real_quotes_are_accepted(quote):
    assert quote_in_text(quote, REVIEW)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "quote",
    ["I omitted the eggs", "I used a whole cup of sugar", "", "...", "I used a half cup of sugar ... I doubled it"],
)
def test_fabricated_or_empty_quotes_are_rejected(quote):
    assert not quote_in_text(quote, REVIEW)

def extractor(*outcomes):
    calls = []

    def parse(**kwargs):
        calls.append(kwargs)
        outcome = outcomes[len(calls) - 1]
        if isinstance(outcome, Exception):

        parsed, refusal = outcome
        return NS(choices=[NS(message=NS(parsed=parsed, refusal=refusal))])

Original scraped recipes in `data/` directory contain `reviews` (and `featured_tweaks`). Enhanced recipes include:

```json
{
  "recipe_id": "10813_enhanced",
  "title": "Best Chocolate Chip Cookies (Community Enhanced)",
  "ingredients": ["1 cup butter, softened", "2 eggs", "1 egg yolk", ...],
  "modifications_applied": [
    {
      "source_review": {
        "text": "I used an ice cream scoop, ... I did add an additional egg yolk to help keep the cookie chewy. ...",
        "reviewer": null,
        "rating": 5,
        "source": "reviews",
        "review_index": 0
      },
      "modification_type": "addition",
      "evidence_quote": "I did add an additional egg yolk to help keep the cookie chewy.",
      "reasoning": "The reviewer added it to keep the cookies chewy.",
      "changes_made": [
        {"type": "ingredient", "from_text": "", "to_text": "1 egg yolk", "operation": "add",
         "line_ref": 3, "match_method": "exact", "match_score": 1.0}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "modifications_skipped": [
    {
      "source_review": {"text": "...", "rating": 5, "source": "reviews", "review_index": 6},
      "modification_type": "quantity_adjustment",
      "evidence_quote": "used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown",
      "status": "tried",
      "outcome": "positive",
      "reasoning": "...",
      "skip_reason": "edit_failed",
      "detail": "conflict: ingredient line '1.5 cups packed brown sugar' was already changed by reviews[1]",
      "proposed_edits": [...]
    }
  ],
  "extraction_failures": [],
  "enhancement_summary": {
    "total_changes": 9,
    "change_types": ["addition", "quantity_adjustment", "removal", "technique_change"],
    "expected_impact": "...",
    "reviews_analyzed": 9,
    "tweaks_extracted": 12,
    "tweaks_applied": 8,
    "tweaks_skipped": 4
  }
}
```

- `source_review.source` + `review_index` point at the exact entry in the recipe file (e.g. `reviews[0]`).
- `line_ref` is the index of the affected line in the original recipe (for an `add`, the line it follows).
- `skip_reason` is one of `evidence_not_in_review`, `not_tried`, `outcome_not_positive`, `no_edits`, `edit_failed`.

## How It Works

The LLM Analysis Pipeline processes recipes in 3 steps:

1. **Tweak Extraction**: Sends **every** review to the LLM (the scraper's `has_modification` keyword flag misses real tweaks, so it is not used as a filter). Each review yields a list of tweaks, one per distinct change, each with a verbatim `evidence_quote`, whether the reviewer `tried` or only `suggested` it, the reviewer's reported `outcome`, and edits that target numbered recipe lines. Output is enforced with a JSON schema (structured outputs).
2. **Recipe Modification**: Applies eligible tweaks to the original recipe:
   - Eligible = the evidence quote really appears in the review, the reviewer tried it, and reported a positive outcome.
   - Order: higher-rated reviews first, then file order; earlier reviews win conflicts.
   - Each edit's target is located by exact substring, then case/whitespace-insensitive substring, then (only if unique and ≥ 0.85 similar) a whole-line fuzzy match. Several matching lines are resolved only by the edit's line number.
   - Each tweak is applied all-or-nothing. Ambiguous targets, missing targets, no-op edits, and edits that would overwrite another review's change are refused.
3. **Enhanced Recipe Generation**: Creates the enhanced version. Every applied change cites its review, evidence quote and original line; every tweak that was not applied is listed with the reason; reviews whose extraction failed are listed too.

Each run produces one enhanced recipe per original recipe that has reviews, with complete attribution showing exactly what changed, what did not, and why.

# Recipe Enhancement Platform

Automatically enhances recipes by analyzing and applying community-tested modifications from AllRecipes.com. Uses LLM processing to extract meaningful recipe tweaks and apply them with full citation tracking.

## Installation

This project uses [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for fast, reliable Python package management.

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.13+
- `uv` package manager

## Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip sync pyproject.toml
```

### Environment Variables

Create a `.env` file in the project root:

```env
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-openai-api-key-here
```

## Usage

### 1. Scrape Recipes (Optional - data already provided)

```bash
uv run python src/scraper_v2.py
```

### 2. Run Recipe Enhancement Pipeline

```bash
cd src

# Test single recipe (chocolate chip cookies)
uv run python test_pipeline.py single

# Process all recipes
uv run python test_pipeline.py all
```

## Output

### Enhanced Recipes

Enhanced recipes are saved in `src/data/enhanced/`:

- `enhanced_[recipe_id]_[recipe-name].json` - Individual enhanced recipes with modifications applied
- `pipeline_summary_report.json` - Summary of all processing results

### Data Structure

Original scraped recipes in `data/` directory contain reviews with `has_modification: true` flags. Enhanced recipes include:

```json
{
  "recipe_id": "10813_enhanced",
  "title": "Best Chocolate Chip Cookies (Community Enhanced)",
  "ingredients": ["1 cup butter", "1 additional egg yolk", ...],
  "modifications_applied": [
    {
      "source_review": {
        "text": "I added an extra egg yolk for chewier texture",
        "rating": 5
      },
      "modification_type": "addition",
      "reasoning": "Improves texture and chewiness",
      "changes_made": [...]
    }
  ],
  "enhancement_summary": {
    "total_changes": 1,
    "change_types": ["addition"],
    "expected_impact": "Chewier texture and improved consistency"
  }
}
```

## How It Works

The LLM Analysis Pipeline processes recipes in 3 steps:

1. **Tweak Extraction**: Selects one random review with modifications and uses GPT-4o-mini to extract structured changes
2. **Recipe Modification**: Applies changes to the original recipe using fuzzy string matching
3. **Enhanced Recipe Generation**: Creates enhanced version with full citation tracking back to source review

Each run produces one enhanced recipe per original recipe, with complete attribution showing exactly what changed and why.

## Development

```bash
# Add dependencies
uv add <package_name>

# Run tests
cd src && uv run python test_pipeline.py single
```

# Recipe Enhancement Platform

Automatically enhances recipes by analyzing and applying community-tested modifications from AllRecipes.com. Uses LLM processing to extract meaningful recipe tweaks and apply them with full citation tracking.

## Installation

This project uses [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for fast, reliable Python package management.

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.13+
- `uv` package manager

## Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip sync pyproject.toml
```

### Environment Variables

Create a `.env` file in the project root:

```env
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-openai-api-key-here
# Optional: any model that supports structured outputs (default gpt-4o-mini)
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
```

## Usage

### 1. Scrape Recipes (Optional - data already provided)

```bash
uv run python src/scraper_v2.py
```

### 2. Run Recipe Enhancement Pipeline

```bash
cd src

# Test single recipe (chocolate chip cookies)
uv run python test_pipeline.py single

# Process all recipes
uv run python test_pipeline.py all
```

## Output

### Enhanced Recipes

Enhanced recipes are saved in `src/data/enhanced/`:

- `enhanced_[recipe_id]_[recipe-name].json` - Individual enhanced recipes with modifications applied
- `pipeline_summary_report.json` - Summary of all processing results

### Data Structure

Original scraped recipes in `data/` directory contain `reviews` (and `featured_tweaks`). Enhanced recipes include:

```json
{
  "recipe_id": "10813_enhanced",
  "title": "Best Chocolate Chip Cookies (Community Enhanced)",
  "ingredients": ["1 cup butter, softened", "2 eggs", "1 egg yolk", ...],
  "modifications_applied": [
    {
      "source_review": {
        "text": "I used an ice cream scoop, ... I did add an additional egg yolk to help keep the cookie chewy. ...",
        "reviewer": null,
        "rating": 5,
        "source": "reviews",
        "review_index": 0
      },
      "modification_type": "addition",
      "evidence_quote": "I did add an additional egg yolk to help keep the cookie chewy.",
      "reasoning": "The reviewer added it to keep the cookies chewy.",
      "changes_made": [
        {"type": "ingredient", "from_text": "", "to_text": "1 egg yolk", "operation": "add",
         "line_ref": 3, "match_method": "exact", "match_score": 1.0}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "modifications_skipped": [
    {
      "source_review": {"text": "...", "rating": 5, "source": "reviews", "review_index": 6},
      "modification_type": "quantity_adjustment",
      "evidence_quote": "used a whole cup of white sugar and 1/2 c of brown",
      "status": "tried",
      "outcome": "positive",
      "reasoning": "...",
      "skip_reason": "edit_failed",
      "detail": "conflict: ingredient line '1.5 cups packed brown sugar' was already changed by reviews[1]",
      "proposed_edits": [...]
    }
  ],
  "extraction_failures": [],
  "enhancement_summary": {
    "total_changes": 9,
    "change_types": ["addition", "quantity_adjustment", "removal", "technique_change"],
    "expected_impact": "...",
    "reviews_analyzed": 9,
    "tweaks_extracted": 12,
    "tweaks_applied": 8,
    "tweaks_skipped": 4
  }
}
```

- `source_review.source` + `review_index` point at the exact entry in the recipe file (e.g. `reviews[0]`).
- `line_ref` is the index of the affected line in the original recipe (for an `add`, the line it follows).
- `skip_reason` is one of `evidence_not_in_review`, `not_tried`, `outcome_not_positive`, `no_edits`, `edit_failed`.

## How It Works

The LLM Analysis Pipeline processes recipes in 3 steps:

1. **Tweak Extraction**: Sends **every** review to the LLM (the scraper's `has_modification` keyword flag misses real tweaks, so it is not used as a filter). Each review yields a list of tweaks, one per distinct change, each with a verbatim `evidence_quote`, whether the reviewer `tried` or only `suggested` it, the reviewer's reported `outcome`, and edits that target numbered recipe lines. Output is enforced with a JSON schema (structured outputs).
2. **Recipe Modification**: Applies eligible tweaks to the original recipe:
   - Eligible = the evidence quote really appears in the review, the reviewer tried it, and reported a positive outcome.
   - Order: higher-rated reviews first, then file order; earlier reviews win conflicts.
   - Each edit's target is located by exact substring, then case/whitespace-insensitive substring, then (only if unique and ≥ 0.85 similar) a whole-line fuzzy match. Several matching lines are resolved only by the edit's line number.
   - Each tweak is applied all-or-nothing. Ambiguous targets, missing targets, no-op edits, and edits that would overwrite another review's change are refused.
3. **Enhanced Recipe Generation**: Creates the enhanced version. Every applied change cites its review, evidence quote and original line; every tweak that was not applied is listed with the reason; reviews whose extraction failed are listed too.

Each run produces one enhanced recipe per original recipe that has reviews, with complete attribution showing exactly what changed, what did not, and why.

## Development

```bash
# Add dependencies
uv add <package_name>

# Run tests
cd src && uv run python test_pipeline.py single
```

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

 "ice cream scoop": {"modification_type":"addition","reasoning":"chewier","edits":[{"target":"ingredients","operation":"add_after","find":"2 eggs","add":"1 additional egg yolk"}]},
